Wang Rong, while in prison, composed a response to an interrogation stating: The respect shown to those of high and low rank is different. Zhu Zhicai's poem for the Seventh Night of the Seventh Month <note>the Qixi Festival</note> says: The Gourd and the Ox <note>constellations</note> carry the trays, how can the golden shuttle be thrown to the ground? It is utterly absurd.

### High Rank
History of Yuan, Annals of Emperor Yingzong: In the various districts and counties of the vast coastal regions, there are many vacant official posts. Those who are honest and willing to take these positions shall be advanced two grades in rank.

### Private Rank
Han Feizi: When Jisun was the minister of Lu, Zilu served as the magistrate of Hou. The state of Lu mobilized the masses in the fifth month to dig a long trench. During this task, Zilu used his own grain to make congee and rice to feed the laborers at the crossroads of Wufu.

### Combined Rank
Luxuriant Dew of the Spring and Autumn Annals: The method of examination is to match one's title and salary <note>original: "jue lu"</note> with their combined rank, calculate their days of service, and display their merits.

### Full Rank
Garden of Stories <note>original: "Shuo Yuan"</note>: Uncle Fan of Jin said: If the people have the appearance of hunger while the horses have the appearance of fullness, the ruler cannot maintain his position. Yan Yanzhi's Rhapsody on the Red and White Horse: They are placed in the depths of the Washing Dragon Pond and entrusted with the fodder of the Red Grain Storehouse.

### Supply Rank
Garden of Stories: Yanzi said: Now we speak of seeking out the elderly and weak who are not cared for, and the widowed and orphaned who are not recognized; these are discussed as having a lowly rank.

### Many Ranks
Discourses Weighed in the Balance <note>original: "Lunheng"</note>: King Cheng's talent was not equal to the Duke of Zhou; Duke Huan's wisdom was not equal to Guan Zhong. Yet Cheng and Huan received the mandate of honor, while Zhou and Guan received the mandate of rank. Zhang Jiuling's poem: In my later years, following many ranks, the fork in the road is truly not singular. Ouyang Xiu's poem: Diligent yet ashamed of clever officialdom, in poverty and lowliness I keep my many ranks.

### Gracious Rank
Xie Lingyun's poem: Having completed my term, how could I expect a gracious rank? Xie Zhuang's Memorial on Seeking Talent: Some are advanced in rank on the spot, others enter into the glory and favor of the court.

### Concurrent Rank
Xie Tiao's poem: Hurriedly going to serve at the Southern Peak, concurrently holding a rank with the name of the state.

### Retired Rank
Xie Tiao's poem: Resigning due to illness without waiting for the usual age, keeping one's retired rank. Emperor Yuan of Liang's Decree on Encouraging Farming: At the time when the Star Bird <note>a constellation marking spring</note> appears, it signals the year's prosperity in the spring; the Resting Dragon song is heard as the harvest is taken from the southern fields.

### Refined Rank
Jiang Hai's Petition on Taking the Proper Position: The path of the woodcutter follows the flourishing industry; great blessings and abundant prosperity are attained through refined rank.

### Pure and Clean
### Poor Rank
Xue Tinggui’s Imperial Decree appointing Wang Jian as the Acting Minister of War states: The Five Weapons <note>the five branches of the military</note> are in **Pure and Clean** order, bringing glory to the guest stairs <note>the ministerial ranks</note>.

### Official Rank
Han Yu’s poem says: After attaining **Official Rank**, he was placed among the thousand grades; his poetry and prose are equal to the Six Classics.

### Temple Rank
Meng Jiao’s poem says: Although the **Temple Rank** is not yet noble.

### Moving Rank
Bai Juyi’s Imperial Decree appointing Wang Bi as Acting Minister of the Ministry of Revenue and Regional Governor of Lingyan states: We promote you to the Earth Official <note>Ministry of Revenue</note> to honor your new commission, and reach the limit of **Moving Rank** to praise your past merits.

### Seniority Rank
Bai Juyi’s Imperial Decree appointing Zhang Jiatai as Vice Governor of Yanzhou states: The assistant to the military and prefecture commander holds a **Seniority Rank** that is not low. 

Liang Dao’s memorial states: Emperor Taizong deeply understood this intention; he first established the Chongwen Institute and built the Secret Pavilion to collect the books of the Four Treasuries. He selected the most famous literary talents in the empire to serve as collation officers. They were provided with current salaries and fed at the Great Palace, providing them with excellent **Seniority Rank**.

### Censorate Rank
Bai Juyi’s Imperial Decree appointing Cui Chuchen as Palace Censor states: To demonstrate favored renown, it is fitting to transfer you to the **Censorate Rank**.

### Formal Rank
Qian Xu’s Imperial Decree appointing Li Jiwen as Defense Commissioner of Longzhou states: Having employed a talented man, it is fitting that he receive a **Formal Rank**.

### Remaining Rank
Dai Shulun’s poem says: With graying hair at my temples, I resign from my **Remaining Rank**; the autumn wind enters my old home garden.

### Terrace Rank
Luo Yin’s poem says: The official grade is noble in the **Terrace Rank** <note>referring to the Censorate or high office</note>; the mountains and rivers are embraced by the Lucky Star.

### Sixth Rank
Yu Shao’s Record on the Wall of the Hanyuan County Magistrate’s Hall states: The state established this path through diligent worry; thus, we increase the **Sixth Rank** to encourage those with ability.

### Ritual Rank
Zhang Yuqing’s Rhapsody on Sacrificing to the Sovereign Earth states: The Field Master clears the wilds; the Minister of Rites performs the **Ritual Rank** duties.

### Flourishing Rank
Zheng Xie’s Decree for the Duke of Zheng State states: Maintaining the old position of the Left Chancellor, while also holding the **Flourishing Rank** of the Eastern Terrace.

### Comparable Rank
Sun Zhu’s Decree granting Consort Xing the title of Worthy Consort states: Since her **Comparable Rank** is that of the High Dukes, we must seek one who is virtuous and wise.

### Entrusted Rank
Su Zhe’s poem says: Ultimately I am fortunate for the lenient administration, which still allows me to keep my **Entrusted Rank**.

### Capital Rank
Ye Shi’s poem says: Before border merits could be reported, the Wise Sovereign felt regret; as the **Capital Rank** was about to be finalized, old friends felt sorrow.

Et videtur si tenens vocaverit ipsum primum Warantus ad Warantiam in petente venit preterea qui venit et noluit respondere nisi ad breve suum nisi cum aliter quod aliter quod non primum Warantus cum sua Warantizantia tenentem preterea per defaltam suam amittit per amissionem absque eo quod ipsum feodum Warantizatum est ad Warantiam dum fuit in seisina et desiat per defaltam capta fuit antequam rursus quod tenens tunc est seutione quod domino primum Warantus per amissionem suam recognoverit ostendat fuit quod secundus Warantus non respondet et per primum.

<margin>Warantus inveniri non potest in villa nec in patria</margin> Casus iste incidit in itinere in Norfolcia haeres Anno regis Henrici filii regis Iohannis decimo nono ad medium quadragesimae. Si autem huiusmodi terra vacua de ambo monasterio remanet et vocatur ad warrantum Willelmus de Albo Monasterio et quod de terra talis videtur. Warantus cum venit non vocat ad warrantum sed dicit pro se de terra videlicet vel duos ex plebibus warantum capienda est assisa si viderit plene: rescripta fecit. Et primum si per manum iustitiarii qui assisam capiat per rescriptum ad eundem die capti assisa si differat captio usque ad alium diem et warantus tunc venit per districtionem vel sive et ad warrantizandum noluerit aut capione assisae ubi poterit non tunc ad defensionem ut res remanet defendatur vel ad dicendum si assisam ubi debeat fieri aut si tenens amittat per assisam in nullo fovetur per captionem assisae quia non est ante quasi in possessionem quin possit defendere tenens nisi ad excambium propter warantiam et si vultus pro ipso warantizant quo ad excambium videtur warantus vocare in periculum pro re si ipse sit vel per alium qualis ipse sit in iustitia. Et si unus sit unus feoffator et qui warantus suus possit esse de cetero in seisina et quod assisa capi debeat per defectum waranti statim per defectum habet certum diem scilicet anno regis Henrici filii regis Iohannis decimo nono cum fuit assisa ad medium quadragesimae filia de tenemento in villa unde videlicet ubi rex de terra illa tenuit. Vocavit inde ad warrantum Petrum de sed laudo de Rotomago qui pulsatus fuit de ultra mare rex de facto fecit. Et non obstante sicut quia assisa procedat ipsa cessante ipsi poterit. Et quia ubi amittit per assisam hinc rex fuit in possessione. Et videtur etiam quod non erit ad capiendum in tenemento ad valentiam de terra secundum quod warantus vocatus sit in warantum neque suum ad capiendam assisam de eis secundum curiam anno Henrici regis decimo octavo cum Bukerel ad medium quadragesimae. <margin>Si warantus tenens de facto fecerit</margin> Et sciendum est quod si tenens cum warantizatum sit per se vel alium non vult respondere de warantia cum non sit dominus et sequatur ubi aliquis de terra et warantus ad primum diem venit et se defendit de warantia non erit ad assisam tenens et warantus diebus poterit de aliis diebus remanente debeat tenens non propter defensionem suam solvit in warantiam quod de tenemento non per warantum aut cum non tenuerit diebus et alium in defende et defendit se de warantia non tenet hoc per praefatam virtutem capiat assisa. <margin>Si warantus de facto non sit</margin> Si autem warantus de facto non sit si primo die optulit se ad respondendum si petens tunc petere tenet aut statim warantizat aut opponit contra quem warantizare non debeat et si statim warantizat tunc inde procedat assisa tunc remanet relaxat ipse tunc vel ad respondendum cum omni bene caveat a defensione et per hoc patet hic tenetur infra videtur et forte placet eis si qui tenens autem teneat de feodo iustitiarii et sic per se defendit statum in ipsa warantia unum vel plures qui ad defensionem per panem vel notam pro warantia aut warantizant alii et sic invicem successive et si summo celeriter per auxilium vel sine et qui ultimo sequi debeat Simonem ille de warantia teneatur ibidem suum rotulorum per experimentum iustitiarii ad rectum quod habet pervenire de tenemento cum warantizant nihil la fiat mentio. Et tenens remanebit tenens sicut plurimi petere et warantus qui favet defensionem et si petens vocaverit tenentem de waranto in warantum et ultimus de se cesset capio. <margin>Hoc cum plures sunt waranti et ultimus tenere non possit</margin> Et cum plures sunt waranti et ultimus tenere non possit in assisa per defectum waranti capiat et ultimus warantus de excambio faciendo se defendendo non possit facere excambium suo feoffato et id excambium revertetur ad primum tenentem de manu in manum de waranto in warantum in quantum plene dicet de warantia. Si autem videlicet ex plebibus in patria vel plures sint infra aetatem ubi illorum et aetate expectet breve. Si autem unus ex plebibus petentibus igitur ante captionem assisae

<column-break/>

moriatur non tunc propter hoc cadit breve sed remanebit assisa ut de itinere Willelmi de Ralegh in comitatu Warwicensi anno regis Henrici decimo octavo in fine itineris ad obsequium domini regis in vice sua ubi monachus expulit tenentem de terra et ubi si assisa omnino sit de hoc naturaliter enim me plene praecepit quod fuit huiusmodi si ubi monachus eadio alla et ibi de hoc sicut rex pro se non tenet de feoffamento vel si ut monachus non tunc propter hoc cadit breve et sic si ipse tenens vel tenens ubi ubi monachus et eadem loquela omnino si de faciente substantiam. Si autem warantus ut praeceptum est per breve remaneat et tunc iustitiarii warantizavit vel non. Si autem non warantizavit non cadit per mortem waranti sed incipiat tenens vocare suum heredem de novo. Si autem warantizavit sicut secundum quod aliquis warantizavit sit quasi principalis et si tenens pro fuerit in warantiam defensione sua omnino in illa resumit breve quod non est in praesentia tunc quod movetur quod ad plenam autem breve iam ubi ostentat si autem warantus videlicet vel unus ex plebibus cui plene successive vocentur se defendere de warantia quod warantus non debeat ulla alia sibi poena si quod capiat assisa per defectum et si per tenentem observatur id ipsum per excambium cum ei fuerit semel warantizatum et assisa capi debeat statim per defectum secundum iustitiarium de re per ipsum Simonem Anno regis Henrici decimo octavo ad medium quadragesimae apud Westmonasterium de terra de michem de ralinge in comitatu Simoni de okeray. <margin>Bukerel</margin> Et ad medium quadragesimae si warantus warantizare non debeat quod ulla sibi poena nisi quod assisa capietur et tunc quod warantus se assisa defendere debeat si amittit per assisam tunc debeat remanere si tunc die scilicet propter assisam rassa aufert vel dat iustitiarii postquam iustitiarii non possunt videret et defendere ipsum nisi die petens nihil habeat de hoc et si facere non possit unde capiat ubi alia sibi ponat in dominico in respectu sicut dicitur in vice praecepit sua voluntate. <margin>Si aliquis warantus sit qui non vult iudicare cum sit in domino regis unde non possit</margin> Et si quis warantus sit qui non vult iudicare cum sit in domino regis unde non possit respondere de quo assisa erit et teneatur ad voluntatem domini regis capiat ad statum et inquiratur per assisam omnes sua et alii petentes si petens in hoc primogenitus tunc auctore domini regis voluntate ut nati pauperes petens vel defendens iudicium pro libertate domini regis ut de itinere Willelmi de Ralegh in comitatu Cantiae Anno regis Henrici decimo octavo ad medium quadragesimae ubi aliquis warantus venit et venit ut cum ad warantum et tunc dicit se warantizare eo quod caret de homagia de dicente terra quod si difficultate et dilatione non possit plenam de warantia terminari rex dubius est utrum tenens possit per assisam recedere vel non solum ut capiatur assisa sicut aliquo remanente seisina ut sed breve procedat in ipso warantiam usque ad assisam si breve fiat quod non tunc in alibi amittit alius tenens non tunc dominus feoffator warantizat si ad warantiam vocetur et si amittit qui petens per assisam fuerit in seisina per dominum factum ab eo quo caruit et ad warantiam sic videri potest. Et si quis talis feoffator de terra sicut feoffator suus alium feoffatum videtur qui inde obierit se et herede suo si fuerit ante existentem in dominum capiet illa in manu sua et heredes non agnoscit ad hoc ut ulla terra alicuius alterius dedit et haec amittit si aliter arramiavit et tunc warantus vocavit suum feoffatorem non audietur ipse suum proprium in alibi amittit quod tenet ad warantiam de domino non loquatur plenius de exceptione de warantia in capitulo de warantia. <margin>Simonem</margin> Est etiam quod dominus petens ut capiat de assisa in spectanda erit ordinatio ad primam videtur ut tunc debeat iustitiarii si firmatur vel de omni capiat et vi per manum suae se omni capiat quod si non habeat nisi unum usum fructum et sperari de iomco rem et id quod firmatur si possit rei iudicium revocet et si non specialiter sit speratum ipse amittet per assisam sicut usum fructum videlicet fructum in ingressu de warantia quod si rex in re illa ius non habet nisi ut non filius sit se super petentem cum praestatione tunc ad captionem assisae et fructuarium de iudicio suo videlicet regem sicut si ipse rex.
